memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Support evidence: while choosing among active multi-night hotel options, Maya explicitly endorsed prioritizing properties with both a pool and an on-site gym, treating a hot tub as an additional but nonessential benefit. The selected $236 hotel satisfies both core amenities and lists a hot tub.

messages.content: I want to settle the North Hills hotel now. Can you compare the real two-night totals, including tax, breakfast, and the rideshares we would actually need? I also need a workable plan for my suitcase on Thursday.

Yes. I will use the 13.25% lodging-tax estimate and the existing $34 airport-to-North Hills and $36 North Hills-to-RDU ride estimates. Before I total everything, is the nightly lodging cap still $250 before tax?
Yes, $250 before tax. The $252 place can stay in the comparison, but I cannot select it unless the rate drops.

Understood. I have three candidates: the $252 hotel beside the client building with breakfast included; the $218 hotel about ten minutes away by car, with breakfast at $16 each morning; and the $236 hotel within a half-mile walk, also with breakfast included but requiring a nonrefundable first-night deposit. I will treat this as one traveler and two breakfasts.
Correct. Also check the pool and exercise options before recommending one.

The current property details show that the $252 hotel has a fitness room but no pool. The $218 hotel has a pool and fitness center but no hot tub listed. The $236 hotel lists an indoor pool, fitness center, and hot tub. Amenity hours can change, so those should still be confirmed directly before purchase.
For multi-night stays, keep prioritizing hotels that have both a pool and an on-site gym. A hot tub is a plus when the rest works, but it should not rule out a better hotel by itself.
That makes the $218 and $236 properties the relevant finalists. The $236 option is the only one of those two currently listing a hot tub, and it remains under the $250 nightly cap.
Show me all three totals anyway. Be explicit about which rides you included.

The $252 hotel costs $504 for two nights plus $66.78 estimated lodging tax, for $570.78. Breakfast is included. Because it is beside the client building, I included only the $34 Tuesday airport ride and the $36 Thursday airport ride. Estimated hotel, breakfast, and local transportation total: $640.78.
That confirms it is over the rate cap even though the overall total is not terrible. What about the cheaper one?

The $218 hotel costs $436 plus $57.77 estimated lodging tax, or $493.77. Two $16 breakfasts add $32. I included the $34 arrival ride, an estimated $11 each way for Wednesday, another $11 ride to the client Thursday morning, and the $36 airport ride Thursday afternoon. That is $103 in rideshares and an estimated combined total of $628.77. Any restaurant sales tax or breakfast gratuity would be additional because only the stated $16 charge is available.
And the walkable $236 property?

Two nights are $472, and estimated lodging tax is $62.54, producing a hotel total of $534.54. Breakfast is included. If you walk to the client site, the only expected rides are $34 from RDU Tuesday and $36 back to RDU Thursday, so the combined estimate is $604.54. That is $24.23 less than the $218 option and $36.24 less than the $252 option.
The deposit is the concern. What exactly is exposed if plans change?

The quoted condition is a first-night deposit that becomes nonrefundable. On the current rate, that exposes $236, and possibly the associated $31.27 lodging tax depending on how the property processes a cancellation. The remaining night should not be assumed refundable until the full terms are displayed. I would verify the deposit charge date, cancellation deadline for night two, and whether tax on the forfeited deposit is retained.
How practical is the half-mile walk compared with the hotel next door? I will have a laptop bag, but not the suitcase during the sessions if the hotel holds it.

The adjacent hotel's route is about two to three minutes and requires only the short entrance-area crossing. From the $236 hotel, the mapped route is roughly half a mile on sidewalks, with one signalized major crossing; allow 9 to 12 minutes each way. It is reasonable with a laptop bag in ordinary weather, but the adjacent property is materially easier in heavy rain. The $218 hotel is not a practical walk and depends on rideshares.
Can the $236 hotel handle the late arrival Tuesday and hold the suitcase after checkout Thursday?

Its front desk confirms 24-hour staffing, so arrival around 8:30 to 9:00 p.m. after the 7:42 landing is acceptable. It also confirms complimentary same-day luggage holding after checkout. Ask the desk to tag the suitcase Thursday morning and note that you expect to retrieve it around 3:40 p.m.; valuables should remain with you.
Does going back to the hotel for the suitcase create a problem for the 5:55 flight?

It still works. If the session ends at 3:30, walk back in about 10 minutes, allow five minutes to collect the tagged bag, and request the airport ride by roughly 3:45. With the earlier 20-to-40-minute North Hills-to-RDU estimate, expected arrival is about 4:05 to 4:25, ahead of the currently displayed 5:10 checked-bag cutoff. Rain or a delayed meeting narrows that margin, so have the ride queued as the session ends.
Choose the $236 property, then. The lower complete total, walk, breakfast, and facilities outweigh the deposit risk. Give me the final numbers and the checks I should make before paying.

Selected hotel: the $236 North Hills property for Tuesday and Wednesday nights. Estimated lodging is $472 plus $62.54 tax, totaling $534.54; breakfast is included. Add $70 for the Tuesday RDU-to-hotel and Thursday hotel-to-RDU rides, for a stay-and-local-transport estimate of $604.54. With the selected $548 nonstop ticket and $80 checked-bag charge, the projected trip total is $1,232.54 before other meals, tips, or rideshare surge pricing. Before paying, confirm the final taxed hotel total; the $236 deposit charge date and exactly what remains refundable; Tuesday late-arrival notation; complimentary Thursday luggage holding; current pool, fitness-center, and hot-tub availability and hours; and the final walking route. For Thursday, check out with the suitcase tagged at the desk, walk to the client site, return immediately after the 3:30 finish, and request the airport ride by about 3:45. Nothing is booked yet.
